notes:
Copilot's multi-agent orchestration feature is /fleet, which the vendor defines as 'parallel subagent execution' (api.schema.json UIExitPlanModeAction.autopilot_fleet) over the SAME in-process subagents scenario 3.1 uses: N concurrent subagent.started lines land in the parent's own events.jsonl, keyed by a per-call toolCallId, and no child session-state/<id>/ directory is ever created. Four of the seven canonical claudecode phases are therefore UNREACHABLE here by agent architecture, not by defect — child_session_birth (transcript_new), parent_linked, the per-child working→ready drain, and children_swept (transcript_removed) — and the 'no journal / no unknown-project phantom session' guard is vacuous because copilot writes no per-run directory or bookkeeping file at all. What this spec CAN assert is the parent arc: ready→working on the fan-out prompt, HELD working across all three children (both subagent events are Skip=true, parser.go:390, and copilot's only turn boundary is the explicit assistant.turn_end), and working→ready only after the last child returns. That arc is correct today, so this cell is NOT known_failing. NOT ASSERTABLE HERE, and the reason this spec looks thinner than the scenario: SubagentCount(parent)=N. The daemon does compute it — the parser's toolCallId-keyed openSubagents set survives concurrency, countOpenSubagents now reads the LIVE parser (metrics/adapter.go:106-163, the #1256 seam fix), and ComputeSubagentSummary (grouped.go:266-300) makes Total=Working=OpenSubagents with no file children — but expected.jsonl's DSL has no subagent-count predicate AND the daemon's recorded events.jsonl carries no metrics vector at all (its keys are only adapter/cwd/file_size/hook_name/kind/new_state/parent_session_id/pid/prev_state/project_dir/reason/seq/session_id/transcript_path/ts). The N-concurrency proof lives in the recipe's verify as a gate over the AGENT store: at least two (target three) subagent.started unmatched at once, and every subagent.completed BEFORE the first assistant.turn_end — the second condition is the mirror image of the 3.2 gate and is what distinguishes this SYNC fan-out from the background case whose held-working defect this cell deliberately does not touch. Single-birth adapter (agent.FilesUnderRoot + sessionIDFromPath key the session to its session-state/<id>/ dir), so the birth is one phase anchored to start UNPINNED. duration_at_least_ms on the working phase bounds the held-working window: 15000ms is a floor chosen well under the recipe's three concurrent `sleep 25` children, not the span itself. model is left unpinned (--model accepts only "auto"; the parent's effective model is resolved at runtime via session.auto_mode_resolved, and the children run claude-haiku-4.5 independently) and cost is unasserted — record fills both from the recording.

RECORDED 2026-08-05 (CLI 1.0.78). BIRTH RE-ANCHORED: the real session is born directly into `working` (commit 3cde4f8d) and a transient proc-<PID> row is minted first, so session_birth and fanout_working are ONE phase.

BOTH FAITHFULNESS GATES PASS, from the recorded events.jsonl:
(a) CONCURRENCY — the three `task` tool.execution_start records land at 15:19:25.822, .822 and .823, i.e. within one millisecond and therefore in a single assistant message, and all three subagent.started (15:19:25.893/.916/.946) precede the first subagent.completed (15:20:00.396). At that point three subagent.started toolCallIds are simultaneously unmatched. This is a real parallel fan-out, not three sequential dispatches.
(b) SYNC — every subagent.completed (15:20:00.396, 15:20:02.335, 15:20:04.973) precedes the FIRST parent assistant.turn_end (15:20:05.322). The parent turn blocked on the children rather than promoting them to background, which is what separates this cell from 3-2.

SUBAGENT RECORDS SHARE THE PARENT'S TRANSCRIPT. Copilot subagents get no session-state directory of their own: their user.message, tool.execution_start and completion records are all appended to the PARENT's events.jsonl, distinguished only by a top-level "agentId". That is why the expected-absent list below holds (no parent_linked events, no child sessions, no child transcripts) and it is also what broke the first attempt at this cell — the driver's turn_count read the three subagent user.message records as three completed parent turns and tore the session down 14s into three 25s children, capturing three subagent.started and zero subagent.completed. turn_count now skips agentId-scoped rows.

The fan-out prompt drives the real <session-id> session straight into working (born there — events.jsonl already holds the open turn) and it STAYS working across the whole concurrent fan-out: no settle to ready while three children are in flight, and no waiting (--allow-all pre-approves every child's bash, so no permission.requested is written). Only after the last child returns does the parent's explicit assistant.turn_end fire: working → ready. Because the fan-out is SYNC (parallel tool calls block the turn), this transition necessarily lands after every subagent.completed — 15:20:07.518 against a last completion at 15:20:04.973 — and the parent's open-subagent count is back to zero.
